title: Florida Senate, District 40
what_it_does: Represents District 40 in the Florida Senate; votes on state laws and the state budget.
verified_ballot_note: On the Nov. 3 ballot. The Florida Division of Elections 2026 general-election candidate list (checked Oct. 7, 2026) shows 3 qualified candidates: Ramiro Orta (No Party Affiliation), Ana Rodriguez (Republican), Jose Stoute (Democrat). An earlier version of this guide marked the seat as decided, based on a report published before candidate qualifying closed on June 12; that was wrong. Source: https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp

candidates.name: Ana Maria Rodriguez
candidates.photo_source: Florida Senate member page (portrait image URL not verified; site blocked in sandbox)
candidates.background: Rodriguez, a Doral Republican, served in the Florida House before winning the Senate in 2020 and re-election in SD 40 in 2022. In 2026 she faces Democrat Jose Stoute and Ramiro Orta (no party affiliation) on the Nov. 3 ballot, per the Florida Division of Elections candidate list.
candidates.ballot_status: Qualified (Florida Division of Elections candidate list, checked Oct. 7, 2026); faces Jose Stoute (D) and Ramiro Orta (NPA) on Nov. 3

taxes.summary: Her campaign site lists cutting taxes and fees as an affordability priority.
taxes.quote: Cut taxes and fees so residents can keep more of what they earn.

sources.title: Miami-Dade County - Ana Maria Rodriguez (campaign website, undated; accessed 2026-10-18)

property_tax.summary: Voted for CS/HJR 1-F (2026), the June 2026 joint resolution that placed Amendment 3 on the ballot to raise the non-school homestead exemption to $250,000 by 2028 and let counties and cities exempt homesteads entirely; because the vote sent the question to voters rather than cutting taxes itself, a vote for it is coded as leaning toward sharply reducing homestead property taxes rather than as full agreement.

sources.title: CS/HJR 1-F (2026) bill page - The Florida Senate

insurance.summary: Voted for SB 2-A (Dec. 2022), the December 2022 property-insurance law that ended one-way attorney fees and assignment of benefits and created a state reinsurance program, a market-based approach; a vote for it is coded as leaning against more direct state intervention.

sources.title: SB 2-A (Dec. 2022) bill page - The Florida Senate

housing.summary: Voted for CS/SB 102 (2023), the 2023 Live Local Act that put $711 million into state housing programs, required local governments to allow multifamily housing in commercial areas when at least 40 percent of units are affordable, and created property-tax exemptions for affordable developments; a vote for it is coded as leaning toward more government action on housing.

sources.title: CS/SB 102 (2023) bill page - The Florida Senate

immigration.summary: Voted for SB 2-C (2025), the February 2025 special-session immigration law that created a State Board of Immigration Enforcement, made entering Florida as an unauthorized immigrant a state crime and required local cooperation with federal detention.

sources.title: SB 2-C (2025) bill page - The Florida Senate

abortion.summary: Voted for SB 300 (2023), the 2023 law limiting most abortions to six weeks of pregnancy.

sources.title: SB 300 (2023) bill page - The Florida Senate

guns.summary: Voted for HB 543 (2023), the 2023 law allowing adults to carry a concealed firearm without a permit.

sources.title: HB 543 (2023) bill page - The Florida Senate

education_choice.summary: Voted for HB 1 (2023), the 2023 law that made every Florida student eligible for a state-funded scholarship usable at private schools or for home education.

sources.title: HB 1 (2023) bill page - The Florida Senate

record.item: Voted for CS/HJR 1-F (2026), the June 2026 joint resolution that placed Amendment 3 on the ballot to raise the non-school homestead exemption to $250,000 by 2028 and let counties and cities exempt homesteads entirely; because the vote sent the question to voters rather than cutting taxes itself, a vote for it is coded as leaning toward sharply reducing homestead property taxes rather than as full agreement.

Voted for SB 2-C (2025), the February 2025 special-session immigration law that created a State Board of Immigration Enforcement, made entering Florida as an unauthorized immigrant a state crime and required local cooperation with federal detention.
Voted for SB 300 (2023), the 2023 law limiting most abortions to six weeks of pregnancy.
Voted for HB 543 (2023), the 2023 law allowing adults to carry a concealed firearm without a permit.
Voted for HB 1 (2023), the 2023 law that made every Florida student eligible for a state-funded scholarship usable at private schools or for home education.
Voted for SB 254 (2023), the 2023 law barring gender-affirming medical treatment for minors and restricting it for adults.
Voted for SB 7050 (2023), the 2023 elections law that raised penalties and shortened deadlines for third-party voter-registration groups and changed vote-by-mail and voter-roll procedures.

Voted for SB 2-A (Dec. 2022), the December 2022 property-insurance law that ended one-way attorney fees and assignment of benefits and created a state reinsurance program, a market-based approach; a vote for it is coded as leaning against more direct state intervention.
Voted for HB 1 (2021), the 2021 Combating Public Disorder law that created new riot-related offenses and penalties and let the state override local cuts to police budgets.
Voted for HB 5 (2022), the 2022 law limiting most abortions to 15 weeks.
Voted for HB 1557 (2022), the 2022 Parental Rights in Education law restricting classroom instruction on sexual orientation and gender identity.
Voted for SB 90 (2021), the 2021 elections law that added identification requirements for mail-ballot requests and limited drop-box hours.

Voted for CS/CS/HB 1645 (2024), the 2024 energy law that removed climate change as a priority of state energy policy, repealed several renewable-energy goals and grant programs, banned offshore wind turbines in state waters and eased regulation of natural-gas pipelines; a vote for it is coded as leaning against promoting renewable energy.

Voted for CS/SB 102 (2023), the 2023 Live Local Act that put $711 million into state housing programs, required local governments to allow multifamily housing in commercial areas when at least 40 percent of units are affordable, and created property-tax exemptions for affordable developments; a vote for it is coded as leaning toward more government action on housing.

candidates.name: Jose Stoute
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: Physician and infectious-disease specialist; professor; retired U.S. Army colonel
candidates.background: Dr. Jose Stoute is a physician and infectious-disease specialist, a professor and a retired U.S. Army colonel, according to his campaign site. He is running as the Democratic candidate in Senate District 40 (Monroe and part of Miami-Dade) on a platform of affordability, keeping politics out of healthcare and classrooms, and immigration changes. His campaign site is published in English, Spanish, Portuguese and Haitian Creole.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

immigration.summary: Stoute's campaign site calls for leaving U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement out of Florida and protecting communities from what it calls fear-based enforcement, and for restoring a fair, functional legal immigration system.
immigration.quote: Protect communities from fear-based enforcement and keep Florida focused on safety, opportunity, and dignity.

sources.title: Jose Stoute for Florida State Senate District 40: The issues that matter (campaign website, undated; read 2026-10-07)

healthcare.summary: Says Florida should expand Medicaid and affordable coverage; as a physician he backs universal health care as a national goal and keeping medical decisions between patients and doctors.
healthcare.quote: I will support Medicaid expansion and affordable coverage while protecting access to preventive care and medications.

sources.title: VOTE411 voter guide (League of Women Voters): Jose Antonio Stoute, State Senator 40 candidate responses (undated; accessed 2026-10-17)

abortion.summary: Supports abortion access through 21 weeks of pregnancy, and later when the patient's life or serious health is at risk or the fetus has a lethal condition.
abortion.quote: I support access to abortion through 21 weeks of pregnancy.

sources.title: VOTE411 voter guide (League of Women Voters): Jose Antonio Stoute, State Senator 40 candidate responses (undated; accessed 2026-10-17)

elections.summary: Opposes barriers for eligible voters; if proof of citizenship is required, wants the state to verify through existing records and make documents free or very low-cost.
elections.quote: I oppose unnecessary barriers that make it harder for eligible citizens to vote.

sources.title: VOTE411 voter guide (League of Women Voters): Jose Antonio Stoute, State Senator 40 candidate responses (undated; accessed 2026-10-17)

housing.summary: Supports relaxing zoning for multifamily housing near jobs and transit, office-to-housing conversions, incentives tied to affordable units, and stronger renter protections against corporate landlords.
housing.quote: I support relaxing unnecessary zoning restrictions to allow more multifamily housing, apartments, townhomes, and condominiums, particularly near employment centers and public transportation.

sources.title: VOTE411 voter guide (League of Women Voters): Jose Antonio Stoute, State Senator 40 candidate responses (undated; accessed 2026-10-17)

growth.summary: Wants more local home rule and room for communities to adopt stronger standards, but also backs relaxing zoning to allow more housing; his answers point both ways on regulating development.
growth.quote: Florida should restore a healthier balance between state authority and local home rule.

sources.title: VOTE411 voter guide (League of Women Voters): Jose Antonio Stoute, State Senator 40 candidate responses (undated; accessed 2026-10-17)

insurance.summary: Calls insurance the more urgent cost problem; supports reforms that increase competition, holding insurers accountable and examining a stronger statewide risk pool.
insurance.quote: I support examining a stronger statewide risk-pooling approach while holding insurers accountable and addressing the underlying costs that drive premiums.

sources.title: VOTE411 voter guide (League of Women Voters): Jose Antonio Stoute, State Senator 40 candidate responses (undated; accessed 2026-10-17)

property_tax.summary: Says insurance needs urgent action while property taxes support schools, public safety and infrastructure and are already limited by homestead protections.
property_tax.quote: Property taxes matter, but homeowners generally understand that those taxes support schools, public safety, infrastructure, and other local services

sources.title: VOTE411 voter guide (League of Women Voters): Jose Antonio Stoute, State Senator 40 candidate responses (undated; accessed 2026-10-17)

other_issues.title: School vaccination requirements
other_issues.summary: Says Florida should keep evidence-based school vaccination requirements and that the state has a legitimate role in setting minimum public-health standards.

sources.title: VOTE411 voter guide (League of Women Voters): Jose Antonio Stoute, State Senator 40 candidate responses (undated; accessed 2026-10-17)
